solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Moving away from the centre, Conservative held to be leftist?

indicators.note: held to be means the abbreviation for Conservative is kept inside the other word

parts.note: radial describes things spreading outwards from a central point, like spokes

explanation.surface: A political commentator asks whether a Tory drifting from the middle ground has become a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving away from the centre' looks like the definition of a political drift, but it supplies RADIAL, which holds C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone far to the left politically is called a radical; the question mark flags that radicals need not be left-wing.

clue.text: Government of cruel person, not at first upsetting yours truly

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting means turning the letters upwards, reading back
not at first means drop the opening letter

parts.note: a tiger is a fierce, cruel person
yours truly refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: A government led by a cruel tyrant distresses the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' clips TIGER to IGER, which 'upsetting' turns into REGI.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system of government, often an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Presented nothing new in old-fashioned wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping means the outer word encloses the others

parts.note: dated means old-fashioned
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gift was presented, nothing new about it, in dated wrapping paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To present something as a gift is to give or donate it.

clue.text: Reform? Measure up, engaging in that difficult task

indicators.note: engaging means the outer word takes the other in

parts.note: to reform is to change

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A reformer urges people to rise to a hard task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform?' looks like a call to action, but it gives the synonym for change; 'up' reads the measure backwards in this down clue, and 'in that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A challenge is a demanding task that tests one's abilities.

clue.text: Tree in a poetic region not cold

indicators.note: not means the letter for cold is taken away

parts.note: clime is a poetic word for a region or climate
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A tree grows in a warm, poetic landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is a tree; it is not the citrus fruit here.

clue.text: One going for run in European country, English person waiting for match?

indicators.note: going for means taking the place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: France is a European country
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A sports fan from a European country, an Englishman, waits for the match to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going for run' says I replaces R in FRANCE, giving FIANCE, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman engaged to be married is waiting for her wedding, the match in the sense of a marriage.

clue.text: In favour of having locks they should make residents very secure

definitions.text: they should make residents very secure

parts.note: for means in favour of
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Supporters of locks say they keep householders safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests door security, but it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongholds protect those inside them, making occupants very safe.

clue.text: Business person's number of years on the books

parts.note: age is a number of years
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A businessman's age appears in the company records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the parts in a down clue; NT is the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent conducts business on behalf of a client, so is a business person.

clue.text: Advance, holding attack: one may fall?

definitions.text: Advance, holding attack: one may fall?

indicators.note: holding means the first word encloses the other

parts.note: to come is to advance or move forward

indicators.note: may fall says the one drops out of the word

parts.note: a raid is an attack
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A soldier advances and presses an attack in which someone might be killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may fall' drops the I (one) from the attack word; the same words also describe a soldier who may be killed, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers advancing together under fire are fellow fighters, any of whom may be killed in action.

clue.text: Old lover making reference to being sexy?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
citing means quoting or referring to

explanation.surface: Someone's former partner keeps bringing up being attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arousing is thrilling; the question mark admits it is only one kind of thrill.

clue.text: Exceptional men I regard with awe ultimately? Not our police!

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order
ultimately points to the final letter of awe

explanation.surface: A British speaker marvels at some impressive men, then realises they are not the local constabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' rearranges MEN I REGARD; 'ultimately' adds the last letter of awe.
explanation.definitionFit: The French armed police force is a foreign force, so from a British setter's viewpoint it is not our police.

clue.text: Host will collect a coat

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a host

explanation.surface: A party host promises to fetch a guest's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of mackintosh, the British word for a raincoat.

clue.text: Courage to get gold or silver, as you might say?

indicators.note: as you might say tells us the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: gold and silver are both metals

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it takes courage to win a gold or silver medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and resolve in the face of difficulty; a synonym for courage.

clue.text: Lengthen piece of writing started by publicist

indicators.note: started by puts the publicist's letters at the front

parts.note: PRO, public relations officer, is a publicist
a tract is a short written essay or pamphlet

explanation.surface: A publicist begins an article and then pads it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to drag it out in time, a synonym for lengthen.

clue.text: The bosses start to mess about, restricting an outstanding person

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter
restricting means enclosing the following letters

parts.note: anent is an old word for about or concerning
an gives the single letter A
a gem is a wonderful person

explanation.surface: The bosses start making a mess, hemming in a star performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not an anagram signal here: it is the dated preposition meaning 'concerning', which 'restricting' wraps round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The managers of an organisation are collectively its directors or bosses.

clue.text: This operator going wrong could get tongue snarled?

indicators.note: going wrong says the letters of the following words have been jumbled

explanation.surface: If this person slipped up mid-operation, a patient's tongue could end up in a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: jumble the two words of the answer and you get TONGUE SNARLED, a fitting image of a slip in the dentist's chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental surgeon operates on teeth and gums, so is a kind of operator.

clue.text: One getting on in classification process that should be fair for everybody

definitions.text: process that should be fair for everybody

indicators.note: in means the first pieces sit inside the other word

parts.note: a rating is a classification
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An elderly person is graded in a fair system.
explanation.definitionFit: Allocating scarce supplies in fixed shares is meant to give everyone an equal portion.

clue.text: Bird looking intently across lake

indicators.note: across means the first word spans the letter for lake, holding it

parts.note: staring means looking intently

explanation.surface: A bird stares hard across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A common speckled songbird.

clue.text: Office worker taking long time -intellectual and volatile

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
an era is a long period of time
mental means relating to the intellect

explanation.surface: An office temp drags things out and turns out to be clever but moody.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone volatile has moods that change sharply and unpredictably.

clue.text: Person coining it is wicked type, not saint, you gathered

indicators.note: gathered means the old form of you is taken in
not means the saint's abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: a monster is a wicked person
ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Someone making a fortune is a villain, no saint, as you gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coining it' suggests getting rich, but here it means minting coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneyer is someone who mints coins, literally coining.

clue.text: Objective of soldier getting in close

indicators.note: getting in means the soldier goes inside the other word

parts.note: local means close by
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier's target is getting into close range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a noun (target) but is the adjective: unbiased, reasoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning that is objective follows sound rational principles rather than feelings.

clue.text: Measure gold in extraterrestrial debris

parts.note: to mete is to measure out
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Scientists measure the gold content of space rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of rock or dust from space that burns up entering the atmosphere.

clue.text: Goes through what batsman scores against number of deliveries

parts.note: in cricket a batsman scores runs
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket statistician compares a batsman's score with the balls bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a fixed set of six balls from one bowler; 'against' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over something is to rehearse or review it quickly, to go through it.

clue.text: Veteran with nothing left to pass on

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pass on is a euphemism for to die

explanation.surface: An old soldier with nothing remaining is about to die.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old person or thing, someone long in service.

clue.text: Chinese food with 50% horse revealed by study

indicators.note: revealed by means the horse half comes after the study, which leads

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: 50% says take half the word

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A study reveals that a Chinese dish contains horsemeat.
explanation.walkthrough: GEE-GEE is a nursery word for a horse, so half of it is GEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Congee is a rice porridge eaten across China and East Asia.

clue.text: Exploiter using mean trick, first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is moved to the end

parts.note: a ruse is a sly trick

explanation.surface: A con artist uses a dirty trick, start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: One who uses others for their own ends exploits them.

clue.text: Woman making old historian lose his head

indicators.note: losing his head means dropping the first letter of the name

parts.note: Livy was a Roman historian

explanation.surface: A woman drives an ancient historian to distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a woman's name, which crosswords often use for 'woman'.

clue.text: What might suggest Garbo's place in the theatre?

parts.note: read as instructions, the words dress (GARB) and circle (O) together spell the film star's name

explanation.surface: Where in a theatre would the film star Greta Garbo sit?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: a garment (GARB) placed round a ring (O) spells GARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: The first raised tier of seats in a theatre, above the stalls.

clue.text: Fellow carries gun? It's a habit

indicators.note: carries means one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: gent, short for gentleman, means a fellow
an arm is a weapon such as a gun

explanation.surface: A man carrying a gun is apparently quite used to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests routine, but here it is a monk's or nun's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a long robe worn by monks and nuns, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Soldier, say, cutting short reign a leader of republicans

indicators.note: cutting means the example abbreviation slices into the other letters
short means lose the last letter

parts.note: to reign is to rule
say means for example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter

explanation.surface: A soldier cuts short a monarch's reign and becomes the head of the republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' clips RULE to RUL; with A and R that gives RULAR, which EG cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army, as opposed to a reservist.
